1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.subject: Tin Woodman

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.subject: Cowardly Lion

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.quote: They found the ladder so heavy they could not pull it up, so the Scarecrow fell off the wall and the others jumped down upon him so that the hard floor would not hurt their feet.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.quote: As they drew near, the cow suddenly gave a kick and kicked over the stool, the pail, and even the milkmaid herself, and all fell on the china ground with a great clatter.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.subject: milkmaid
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.statement: The milkmaid picks up the leg and leads her cow away.
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.quote: She picked up the leg sulkily and led her cow away, the poor animal limping on three legs.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.subject: Dorothy

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.subject: china people
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.statement: Broken china people and animals can be taken to the mender's shop and glued on again.
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.quote: My cow has broken her leg, and I must take her to the mender’s shop and have it glued on again.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.subject: china people
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.statement: A mended china person is never so pretty after being mended.
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.quote: Oh, yes; but one is never so pretty after being mended, you know,

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.subject: china people
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.statement: Whenever china people are taken away their joints stiffen and they can only stand straight and look pretty.
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.quote: But whenever any of us are taken away our joints at once stiffen, and we can only stand straight and look pretty.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.subject: china people
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.statement: In their own country china people can talk and move around as they please.
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-20-the-d.quote: You see, here in our country we live contentedly, and can talk and move around as we please.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-21-the-l.statement: Cowardly Lion asks the beasts what their trouble is.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-21-the-l.subject: Cowardly Lion
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-21-the-l.statement: Cowardly Lion is King of the animals of the forest.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.statement: The Scarecrow walks boldly forward to cross the hill.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.statement: Hammer-Heads shoot their heads forward on stretching necks to strike people.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.subject: Cowardly Lion
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.statement: The Cowardly Lion dashes up the hill and is struck rolling down the hill.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.statement: Dorothy helps the Scarecrow to his feet.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.subject: Dorothy
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.statement: Dorothy summons the Winged Monkeys with the Golden Cap.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.subject: Winged Monkeys
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.statement: The Winged Monkeys carry Dorothy and her comrades safely over the hill and set them down in the country of the Quadlings.
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.quote: which carried Dorothy and her comrades safely over the hill and set them down in the beautiful country of the Quadlings.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.subject: Dorothy
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.statement: Dorothy cannot summon the Winged Monkeys again.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.subject: Glinda
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.statement: Glinda is the Good Witch who rules the South Country.
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.quote: “To see the Good Witch who rules here,” she answered.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.subject: Glinda
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-22-the-c.statement: Glinda admits Dorothy and the others at once.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.subject: Glinda
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.quote: Her dress was pure white but her eyes were blue, and they looked kindly upon the little girl.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.subject: Glinda
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.quote: Her hair was a rich red in color and fell in flowing ringlets over her shoulders.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.subject: Golden Cap
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.statement: The Golden Cap lets its holder command the Winged Monkeys three times.
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.quote: indeed, it is of no use to me now, and when you have it you can command the Winged Monkeys three times.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.subject: Silver Shoes
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.statement: The Silver Shoes can carry you to any place in the world in three steps, and each step will be made in the wink of an eye.
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.quote: And one of the most curious things about them is that they can carry you to any place in the world in three steps, and each step will be made in the wink of an eye.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.subject: Silver Shoes
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.statement: To use the Silver Shoes you knock the heels together three times and command the shoes to carry you wherever you wish to go.
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.quote: All you have to do is to knock the heels together three times and command the shoes to carry you wherever you wish to go.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.subject: Dorothy
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.statement: Dorothy gives the Golden Cap to Glinda.
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.quote: Dorothy then gave her the Golden Cap, and the Witch said to the Scarecrow, “What will you do when Dorothy has left us?”

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.subject: Scarecrow
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.quote: for Oz has made me its ruler and the people like me.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.subject: Dorothy
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.statement: Dorothy commands the Silver Shoes to take her home to Aunt Em.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.subject: Dorothy
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.statement: Dorothy is on the broad Kansas prairie.

1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.subject: Silver Shoes
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.statement: The Silver Shoes were lost forever in the desert.
1900-the-wonderful-wizard-of-oz-23-glind.quote: For the Silver Shoes had fallen off in her flight through the air, and were lost forever in the desert.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-01-tip-man.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-01-tip-man.quote: for old Mombi often declared that his whole name was Tippetarius;

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-01-tip-man.statement: Mombi has gone to a village to buy groceries.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-01-tip-man.statement: Tip carves a pumpkin to make two round eyes, a three-cornered nose, and a new-moon mouth.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-01-tip-man.quote: With the point of his knife he made two round eyes, a three-cornered nose, and a mouth shaped like a new moon.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-01-tip-man.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-01-tip-man.statement: Tip builds a wooden man with sapling limbs jointed to a bark body.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-01-tip-man.quote: he carefully jointed the limbs and fastened them to the body with pegs whittled into shape with his knife.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-01-tip-man.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-01-tip-man.statement: Tip dresses the wooden man in purple trousers, a red shirt, and a pink vest.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-01-tip-man.quote: These he carried away to his man and succeeded, although the garments did not fit very well, in dressing the creature in a jaunty fashion.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-01-tip-man.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-01-tip-man.statement: Tip names the wooden man Jack Pumpkinhead.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-01-tip-man.quote: I will name the fellow ‘Jack Pumpkinhead!'

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.statement: Tip brings Jack to the bend in the road.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.statement: Tip repairs Jack's fallen-off arm with a new stouter shoulder pin.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.quote: and afterward, by whittling a new and stouter pin for the shoulder-joint, he repaired the injury so successfully that the arm was stronger than before.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.statement: Mombi trades important secrets of magic with a crooked wizard.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.quote: She had met a crooked wizard who resided in a lonely cave in the mountains, and had traded several important secrets of magic with him.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.statement: Mombi sprinkles the Powder of Life over Jack's pumpkin head.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.statement: Mombi chants Weaugh, Teaugh and Peaugh to animate Jack.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.statement: Jack speaks reproachfully after coming to life.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.quote: Of course they are; I made ’em myself,

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.statement: Mombi brews a potion to transform Tip into a marble statue.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-02-the-mar.subject: Land of Oz

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-03-the-fli.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-03-the-fli.statement: Tip takes the Powder of Life with him when he runs away.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-03-the-fli.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-03-the-fli.statement: Tip frees Jack Pumpkinhead from the cow-stable stall.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-03-the-fli.quote: He retraced his steps to the cow-stable and opened the door of the stall where the pumpkin-headed man had been left.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.statement: The Scarecrow ordered the Saw-Horse to carry them to the Tin Woodman through the rebels.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.quote: he must make a dash through the ranks of the rebels and carry us to my friend the Tin Woodman,

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.subject: Soldier with the Green Whiskers
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.statement: The Soldier tied all three riders together and lashed them to the Saw-Horse.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.quote: The Soldier now returned with a long line and tied all three firmly together, also lashing them to the body of the Saw-Horse; so there seemed little danger of their tumbling off.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.subject: Saw-Horse
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.statement: The Saw-Horse bowled over the new Guardian of the Gate.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.quote: As for the Saw-Horse, he made a wonderful record upsetting a fruit cart, overturning several meek looking men, and finally bowling over the new Guardian of the Gate—a fussy little fat woman appointed by General Jinjur.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.subject: Guardian of the Gates
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.statement: The Guardian of the Gate was appointed by General Jinjur.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.quote: As for the Saw-Horse, he made a wonderful record upsetting a fruit cart, overturning several meek looking men, and finally bowling over the new Guardian of the Gate—a fussy little fat woman appointed by General Jinjur.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.statement: Tip's prick wound is in his left arm.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.quote: Tip got one small prick in his left arm, which smarted for an hour afterward; but the needles had no effect upon the Scarecrow or Jack Pumpkinhead, who never even suspected they were being prodded.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.subject: Saw-Horse
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.statement: The Saw-Horse dashed outside the walls of the Emerald City along the road to the West.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.quote: Once outside the walls of the Emerald City he dashed along the road to the West with fast and violent leaps that shook the breath out of the boy and filled the Scarecrow with wonder.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.subject: Saw-Horse
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.statement: The Saw-Horse leaped and launched its riders into the river water.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-09-the-sca.quote: without a pause the wooden steed gave one final leap and launched them all in mid-air.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: Tip shouts to the Saw-Horse to keep still.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: Keep still, you fool! Keep still!

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Saw-Horse
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: The Saw-Horse floats calmly upon the surface of the river.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: The horse at once ceased struggling and floated calmly upon the surface, its wooden body being as buoyant as a raft.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: Tip orders the Saw-Horse to paddle toward the shore.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: Paddle with your legs toward the shore.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Saw-Horse
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: The Saw-Horse reaches the opposite river bank.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: The horse obeyed, and although their progress was slow they finally reached the opposite river bank at a place where it was low enough to enable the creature to scramble upon dry land.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: Tip cuts the cords that bound the riders to the wooden horse.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: With some difficulty the boy managed to get his knife out of his pocket and cut the cords that bound the riders to one another and to the wooden horse.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Jack Pumpkinhead
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: Jack Pumpkinhead loses his pumpkin head in the river.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: but the pumpkin head was gone, and only the sharpened stick that served for a neck was visible.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: Tip retrieves Jack's pumpkin head from the river with his pole.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: the boy was able to reach it with his pole and draw it to the shore.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: Tip replaces the pumpkin head upon Jack's neck.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: ran with it to Jack and replaced the head upon the man’s neck.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: Tip removes the Scarecrow's straw and spreads it in the sun to dry.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: So he carefully removed the straw from the King’s body and legs, and spread it out in the sun to dry.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: Tip stuffs the Scarecrow into shape and smooths out his face.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: When this had been accomplished he stuffed the Scarecrow into symmetrical shape and smoothed out his face so that he wore his usual gay and charming expression.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: Tip tells the Saw-Horse to go slowly.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: Go slowly, for now there is no danger of pursuit,

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: The Scarecrow once saved Dorothy from the Stinging Bees of the Wicked Witch of the West.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: It was upon this grassy knoll that I once saved Dorothy from the Stinging Bees of the Wicked Witch of the West.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman are friends.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: I am anxious to greet my friend the Tin Woodman.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Winged Monkeys
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: The Winged Monkeys are now the slaves of Glinda.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: the Winged Monkeys are now the slaves of Glinda the Good

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.statement: Tip sleeps on the grass using the Scarecrow for a pillow.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-10-the-jou.quote: He then stretched himself upon the grass and, using the stuffed form of the Scarecrow for a pillow, was presently fast asleep.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman are old friends.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: How delighted I shall be to see my old friend the Tin Woodman again!

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: The Tin Woodman is the Emperor of the Winkies.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: Is the Tin Woodman the Emperor of the Winkies?

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: The Tin Woodman prefers to be termed Emperor rather than King.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: it pleases him to be termed Emperor rather than King.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: The Tin Woodman's body is nickel-plated.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: Our mighty Emperor has lately caused himself to be nickel-plated.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: The Tin Woodman's heart lies in his left breast.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: You will observe this engraved star upon my left breast.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: The Scarecrow plucked a double-handful of ripe berries from bushes nearby.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: Tip awoke soon after dawn, but the Scarecrow had already risen and plucked, with his clumsy fingers, a double-handful of ripe berries from some bushes near by.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: Tip ate the berries for breakfast.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: These the boy ate greedily, finding them an ample breakfast, and afterward the little party resumed its Journey.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: The Tin Woodman rushed in and caught the Scarecrow in a close embrace.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: And then the door burst open and Nick Chopper rushed into their midst and caught the Scarecrow in a close and loving embrace that creased him into many folds and wrinkles.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: The Tin Woodman rubbed his polishing paste onto the Scarecrow while welcoming him.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: But, alas! the face of the Scarecrow and many portions of his body bore great blotches of putz-pomade; for the Tin Woodman, in his eagerness to welcome his friend, had quite forgotten the condition of his toilet and had rubbed the thick coating of paste from his own body to that of his comrade.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: The Scarecrow introduced Tip and Jack Pumpkinhead to the Tin Woodman.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: The Scarecrow, with great politeness, introduced Tip and Jack Pumpkinhead, and the latter personage seemed to interest the Tin Woodman greatly.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: Tip brought the Saw-Horse alive with a magic powder.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: I did it with a magic powder,

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: The girls of Oz rose in revolt and drove the Scarecrow out of the Emerald City.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: for the girls of Oz have risen in revolt and driven me out of the emerald City.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: The Tin Woodman agreed to recapture the Emerald City and restore the Scarecrow to his throne.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: we will go at once and recapture the Emerald City and place the Scarecrow again upon his throne.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: Tip mended Jack Pumpkinhead's wooden limbs and made them stronger.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: While this was being done Tip mended the wooden limbs of Jack Pumpkinhead and made them stronger than before, and the Saw-Horse was also inspected to see if he was in good working order.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.statement: The Tin Woodman led the return journey to the Emerald City bearing his gleaming axe, while Jack rode the Saw-Horse and Tip and the Scarecrow walked beside him.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-11-a-nicke.quote: Then bright and early the next morning they set out upon the return Journey to the emerald City, the Tin Woodman bearing upon his shoulder a gleaming axe and leading the way, while the Pumpkinhead rode upon the Saw-Horse and Tip and the Scarecrow walked upon either side to make sure that he didn’t fall off or become damaged.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Jinjur
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: Jinjur commands the Army of Revolt.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: Now, General Jinjur—who, you will remember, commanded the Army of Revolt—was rendered very uneasy by the escape of the Scarecrow from the Emerald City.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Jinjur
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: Jinjur sends for Mombi and promises her large rewards to assist the rebel army.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: So Jinjur sent post-haste for old Mombi, the witch, and promised her large rewards if she would come to the assistance of the rebel army.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: Mombi travels to the Emerald City to assist Jinjur in defeating the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: Mombi was furious at the trick Tip had played upon her as well as at his escape and the theft of the precious Powder of Life; so she needed no urging to induce her to travel to the Emerald City to assist Jinjur in defeating the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, who had made Tip one of their friends.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: Tip played a trick on Mombi, escaped her, and stole the Powder of Life.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: Mombi was furious at the trick Tip had played upon her as well as at his escape and the theft of the precious Powder of Life; so she needed no urging to induce her to travel to the Emerald City to assist Jinjur in defeating the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, who had made Tip one of their friends.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: Mombi locks herself in a small room high up in a tower to work magic to prevent the return of the Scarecrow and his companions.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: Mombi had no sooner arrived at the royal palace than she discovered, by means of her secret magic, that the adventurers were starting upon their Journey to the Emerald City; so she retired to a small room high up in a tower and locked herself in while she practised such arts as she could command to prevent the return of the Scarecrow and his companions.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: who had made Tip one of their friends.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: Tin Woodman is friends with Tip.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: who had made Tip one of their friends.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: The Tin Woodman advances with swinging axe to cut down the sunflower stalks.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: I ought to know by heart and every step of this Journey, yet I fear we have already lost our way.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Saw-Horse
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: The Saw-Horse steps into a rabbit hole, falls, and breaks its leg short off.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: For when his leg was pulled from the rabbit hole it was found to be broken short off, and must be replaced or repaired before he could go a step farther.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: The Tin Woodman catches Jack Pumpkinhead's pumpkin head as it descends and saves it from injury.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: The Pumpkinhead was pitched high into the air, and his history would probably have ended at that exact moment had not the Tin Woodman skillfully caught the pumpkin as it descended and saved it from injury.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: The Scarecrow concludes to take their direction from the sun.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: but old Mombi had so changed the appearance of the landscape that they would surely have been lost had not the Scarecrow wisely concluded to take their direction from the sun.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: sun
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: No witchcraft can change the course of the sun.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: For no witch-craft could change the course of the sun, and it was therefore a safe guide.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Woggle-Bug
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.value: MR. H. M. WOGGLE-BUG, T. E.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: The Woggle-Bug's full name on his card is MR. H. M. WOGGLE-BUG, T. E.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: MR. H. M. WOGGLE-BUG, T. E.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Woggle-Bug
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: H. M. in the Woggle-Bug's name means Highly Magnified.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: “‘H. M.’ means Highly Magnified,” returned the Woggle-Bug, proudly.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Woggle-Bug
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: T. E. in the Woggle-Bug's name means Thoroughly Educated.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: To be more explicit, the initials mean that I am Thoroughly Educated.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.subject: Woggle-Bug
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.statement: The Woggle-Bug standing upright appears fully as tall as the Tin Woodman.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-12-mr-h-m-.quote: Standing upright before our amazed friends the Woggle-Bug appeared to be fully as tall as the Tin Woodman; and surely no bug in all the Land of Oz had ever before attained so enormous a size.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.subject: tailor
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.statement: Tailors have nine lives, like cats.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.quote: tailors having, like cats, nine lives, as you probably know.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.subject: Jack Pumpkinhead
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.statement: Jack Pumpkinhead is the child of Tip.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.subject: Professor Nowitall
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.statement: Professor Nowitall catches Woggle-Bug between his thumb and forefinger.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.quote: before I could escape he had caught me between his thumb and forefinger.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.subject: Woggle-Bug
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.statement: Woggle-Bug escapes unnoticed to a grove of trees near the school-house.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.quote: I calmly walked out of the school-house, turned a corner, and escaped unnoticed to a grove of trees that stood near

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.subject: Woggle-Bug
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.statement: Woggle-Bug saves the ninth life of a tailor.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.quote: I had the good fortune to save the ninth life of a tailor

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.statement: Tin Woodman amputates Jack Pumpkinhead's left leg.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.quote: he submitted to having his left leg amputated by the Tin Woodman

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.statement: Scarecrow leads the party advancing toward the Emerald City.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.quote: following the lead of the Scarecrow, they all advanced in the direction of the Emerald City.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.subject: Woggle-Bug
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.statement: Woggle-Bug intends to visit the Emerald City to give lectures on the Advantages of Magnification.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.quote: it is my intention soon to visit the Emerald City and arrange to give a course of lectures to select audiences on the ‘Advantages of Magnification.’

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.subject: Woggle-Bug
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-13-a-highl.quote: That is why I place ‘T.E.’ Thoroughly Educated upon my cards

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Saw-Horse
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: The Saw-Horse limped because his new leg was too long.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: They soon discovered that the Saw-Horse limped, for his new leg was a trifle too long.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: The Tin Woodman chopped the Saw-Horse's new leg down with his axe.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: So they were obliged to halt while the Tin Woodman chopped it down with his axe, after which the wooden steed paced along more comfortably.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: The Tin Woodman called the Queen of the Field Mice by blowing his silver whistle.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: So the Tin Woodman blew a shrill note upon a silver whistle that hung around his neck, and presently a tiny grey mouse popped from a near-by hole and advanced fearlessly toward them.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Queen of the Field Mice
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: The Queen of the Field Mice and the Tin Woodman are old friends.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: For the Tin Woodman had once saved her life, and the Queen of the Field Mice knew he was to be trusted.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: The Scarecrow carried twelve field mice hidden in the straw of his breast.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: but the field mice obeyed without hesitation, running one after the other to the Scarecrow and hiding themselves in the straw of his breast.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Queen of the Field Mice
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: The Queen of the Field Mice guided the travelers to the Emerald City.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: Then they resumed their journey, the little grey Queen of the Field Mice running swiftly ahead and then pausing until the travelers drew near, when away she would dart again.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: Mombi created a seeming rushing river to bar the travelers' way.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: For when they came to the banks of a rushing river that threatened to bar their way the little Queen kept steadily on, passing through the seeming flood in safety; and our travelers followed her without encountering a single drop of water.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: Mombi created a seeming high granite wall to oppose the travelers.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: But the grey Field Mouse walked straight through it, and the others did the same, the wall melting into mist as they passed it.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: Mombi created forty whirling roads to bewilder the travelers.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: But the Queen called for them to follow her and darted off in a straight line; and when they had gone a few paces the whirling pathways vanished and were seen no more.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: Mombi sent a sheet of crackling flame over the meadow to consume the travelers.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: She sent a sheet of crackling flame rushing over the meadow to consume them; and for the first time the Scarecrow became afraid and turned to fly.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: The Scarecrow turned to fly from the seeming fire.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: and for the first time the Scarecrow became afraid and turned to fly.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Saw-Horse
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: The Saw-Horse turned to flee from the seeming fire.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: “I’m off, too!” cried the Saw-Horse, turning and prancing with agitation;

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Saw-Horse
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: The Saw-Horse's dry wood would burn like kindlings.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: “for my wood is so dry it would burn like kindlings.”

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: Fire would destroy the Scarecrow very quickly.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: “If that fire reaches me I will be gone in no time!” said he, trembling until his straw rattled.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: The Tin Woodman shouted to the party to look at the Field Mouse to show the fire was a deception.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: “Look at the Field Mouse!” he shouted.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: magic
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: All magic is unnatural, and for that reason is to be feared and avoided.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: “All magic is unnatural, and for that reason is to be feared and avoided.”

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.subject: Queen of the Field Mice
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.statement: The Queen of the Field Mice darted away home after guiding the travelers to the Emerald City.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-14-old-mom.quote: “I am always pleased to be of service to my friends,” answered the Queen, and in a flash she had darted away upon her journey home.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.statement: The Tin Woodman is at the Emerald City and advances on its gate.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.quote: he advanced upon the gate, and the others followed him without hesitation.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.statement: The Scarecrow is at the Emerald City marching toward the royal palace.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.quote: our travelers passed the gates in safety and marched down the green marble pavement of the wide street toward the royal palace.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.subject: Jinjur
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.statement: Jinjur is seated in the throne in the Emerald City.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.quote: Seated within the glittering throne was General Jinjur, with the Scarecrow’s second-best crown upon her head, and the royal sceptre in her right hand.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.subject: Jinjur
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.statement: Jinjur is the Queen after taking the throne.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.quote: I have taken it, as you see; so just now I am the Queen

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.statement: The Tin Woodman is disarmed when his axe is snatched from his grasp.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.quote: The Tin Woodman’s axe was snatched from his grasp by some person behind him

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.statement: The Scarecrow and his comrades are made prisoners by Jinjur's Army of Revolt.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.quote: they found themselves surrounded by the Army of Revolt, the girls bearing in either hand their glistening knitting-needles.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.statement: Tip belongs to old Mombi and must be restored to her keeping.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.quote: the boy, who belongs to old Mombi and must be restored to her keeping.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.subject: Jinjur
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.statement: Jinjur orders the Scarecrow and his companions destroyed except for Tip.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.quote: I shall order you all to be destroyed.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.statement: The Scarecrow releases mice from his breast to frighten the Army of Revolt.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.quote: a tiny grey mouse leaped from his bosom to the floor and scampered away between the feet of the Army of Revolt.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.subject: Jinjur
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.statement: Jinjur flees the throne room to the city gates.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.quote: poor Jinjur shot clear over the head of the Scarecrow and escaped through an archway—never pausing in her wild career until she had reached the city gates.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.statement: The Scarecrow and his friends bar the entrances to the palace by closing and locking the heavy doors.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-15-the-pri.quote: ran to the various entrances of the royal palace and closed the heavy doors, bolting and locking them securely.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.subject: Powder of Life
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.statement: The Powder of Life will make anything live that is sprinkled with it.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.quote: I guess it will make anything live that is sprinkled with it; but there’s only about one dose left.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.statement: Mombi brought Jack Pumpkinhead to life with the Powder of Life.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.quote: She brought Jack to life with it, and afterward I used it to bring the Saw-Horse to life.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.statement: Tip brought the Saw-Horse to life with the Powder of Life.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.quote: She brought Jack to life with it, and afterward I used it to bring the Saw-Horse to life.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.subject: Wizard of Oz
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.statement: The Wizard of Oz escaped in a balloon.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.quote: The Wonderful Wizard escaped in a balloon,

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.quote: You ought to be glad that I made you at all.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.statement: The Tin Woodman fitted a carved mahogany table leg onto Jack Pumpkinhead.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.quote: So the Tin Woodman knocked a mahogany center-table to pieces with his axe and fitted one of the legs, which was beautifully carved, on to the body of Jack Pumpkinhead, who was very proud of the acquisition.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.subject: Wizard of Oz
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.statement: The Wizard passed the crown to the Scarecrow.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.quote: The former King of this City, who was named Pastoria, lost the crown to the Wonderful Wizard, who passed it on to me.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.statement: The Scarecrow proposed escaping through the air.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-16-the-sca.quote: We must escape through the air!

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Woggle-Bug
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: The Woggle-Bug carried the Gump's head up the stairs to the roof.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: the insect had carried up the stairs to the roof.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: Tip brought a large upholstered sofa to the roof with the aid of the Saw-Horse.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: Tip, with the aid of the Saw-Horse, had brought a large, upholstered sofa to the roof.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Jack Pumpkinhead
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: Jack Pumpkinhead brought a broom to the roof.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: The Pumpkinhead had brought a broom, which was the first thing he saw.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: The Scarecrow brought a coil of clothes-lines and ropes to the roof.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: The Scarecrow arrived with a coil of clothes-lines and ropes

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: The Tin Woodman cut four great spreading leaves from a huge palm-tree.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: where he had cut four great, spreading leaves from a huge palm-tree that was the pride of all the inhabitants of the Emerald City.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: royal palm-tree
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: The penalty for chopping leaves from the royal palm-tree is to be killed seven times and afterward imprisoned for life.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: the penalty for chopping leaves from the royal palm-tree is to be killed seven times and afterward imprisoned for life.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: Tip and the Saw-Horse fetched a second sofa to the roof.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: So Tip and the Saw-Horse managed, with much labor, to get the second sofa to the roof

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: The Tin Woodman fastened the Gump's head to one end of the sofas.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: and then Nick Chopper fastened the Gump’s head to one end.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: The Tin Woodman fastened the palm-leaves to the sofas as wings.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: So he fastened the palm-leaves to the sofas, two on each side.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: The Tin Woodman fastened the broom to the back end of the sofa body for a tail.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: and he fastened it firmly to the back end of the sofa body.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: Tip sprinkled the Thing with powder to bring it to life.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: Very carefully he began sprinkling the Thing with the precious powder.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: Tip spoke the three cabalistic words to bring the Thing to life.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: Tip did not hesitate an instant in speaking the three cabalistic words

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: Tip had heard Old Mombi pronounce the magic words.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: Having heard old Mombi pronounce the magic words

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: Tip had previously succeeded in bringing the Saw-Horse to life.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: having also succeeded in bringing the Saw-Horse to life

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Gump
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: The Thing rose slowly from the roof and mounted into the air.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: the Thing rose slowly from the roof and mounted into the air.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.subject: Gump
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.statement: The Gump obeyed Tip and settled back upon the roof.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-17-the-ast.quote: And the Gump obeyed, slowly and gracefully waving its four wings in the air until the Thing had settled once more upon the roof and become still.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: Glinda
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: Glinda the Good rules the South Country.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.quote: In the South Country rules a very delightful Queen called Glinda the Good, who I am sure will gladly receive us,

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: Gump
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: The Gump agrees to carry the party through the air wherever they wish to go.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: The Scarecrow suggests going to Glinda the Good to ask her advice.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.quote: “Let us go to her and ask her advice.”

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: Tip commands the Gump to fly southward low enough to escape houses and trees.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.quote: “be kind enough to fly with us to the Southward; and do not go higher than to escape the houses and trees, for it makes me dizzy to be up so far.”

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: Gump
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: The Gump turns toward the South and soars swiftly away.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.quote: the Gump turned toward the South and soared swiftly and majestically away.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: pepper-box
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: The pepper-box has a false bottom.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.quote: the thing certainly has a false bottom.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: pepper-box
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: The cavity below the pepper-box false bottom contains three silver pills and a folded paper.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.quote: And in the cavity below were three silver pills, with a carefully folded paper lying underneath them.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: Wishing Pills
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: Swallow one wishing pill, count seventeen by twos, make a Wish, and the Wish will immediately be granted.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.quote: The Wish will immediately be granted.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: Land of Oz
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: Houses in the Land of Oz are dome-shaped.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.quote: instead of being dome-shaped—as they all are in the Land of Oz—had slanting roofs that rose to a peak in the center.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: Gump
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: The Gump breaks off both his right wings against the sharp edge of the rock and tumbles down the cliff.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.quote: breaking off both his right wings against the sharp edge of the rock and then tumbling over and over down the cliff.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: The travelers fall into a monster Jackdaw nest in a hollow ledge of rock.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.quote: underneath them was a monster nest, built by a colony of Jackdaws in a hollow ledge of rock;

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: Woggle-Bug
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: The Woggle-Bug presents a diamond necklace to the Tin Woodman.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.quote: the Woggle-Bug presented it to him with a graceful speech,

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: The Tin Woodman hangs the diamond necklace around his neck.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.quote: the Woodman hung it around his neck with much pride,

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: The Tin Woodman takes the Scarecrow to pieces except his head and scatters the straw over Tip and the Woggle-Bug to hide them.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.quote: then took the Scarecrow to pieces (all except his head) and scattered the straw over Tip and the Woggle-Bug, completely covering their bodies.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.subject: Jackdaws
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.statement: The Jackdaws fly down upon the intruders in their nest with screams of rage.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-18-in-the-.quote: Perceiving the intruders in their nest the birds flew down upon them with screams of rage.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The Tin Woodman fights the Jackdaws with his axe.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: His axe fairly flashed among the Jackdaws,

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Saw-Horse
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The Saw-Horse kicks out with his wooden legs to beat off the Jackdaws.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: kicked out so viciously with his wooden legs that he beat off as many assailants as did the Woodman’s axe

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Gump
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The Gump waves the two wings remaining on the left side of its body.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: the Gump began wildly waving the two wings remaining on the left side of its body.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The Scarecrow loses all the straw that stuffs his body to the Jackdaws.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: not a vestige of straw remained.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: Tip suggests stuffing the Scarecrow with money.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: Why not stuff him with money?

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The Scarecrow's left leg and boot are stuffed with five-dollar bills.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: The Scarecrow’s left leg and boot were stuffed with five-dollar bills;

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The Scarecrow's right leg is stuffed with ten-dollar bills.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: his right leg was stuffed with ten-dollar bills,

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The Scarecrow's body is filled with fifties, one-hundreds and one-thousands.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: his body so closely filled with fifties, one-hundreds and one-thousands that he could scarcely button his jacket with comfort.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Saw-Horse
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The Saw-Horse suggests starting counting at a half of one to count to seventeen by twos.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: Why not start counting at a half of one?

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: Tip selects one of the pills and swallows it.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: Tip selected one of the pills and swallowed it.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: Tip wishes that he'd never swallowed the pill.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: I wish I’d never swallowed that pill!

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Woggle-Bug
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The Woggle-Bug swallows one of the wishing pills.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Woggle-Bug
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The Woggle-Bug wishes the Gump's broken wings mended and as good as new.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: I wish the Gump’s broken wings mended, and as good as new!

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Gump
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The Gump is repaired and able to fly again.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: the Gump lay before them in perfect repair, and as well able to fly through the air as when it had first been brought to life on the roof of the palace.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Wishing Pills
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: Each wishing pill is good for one wish.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: each pill is good for a wish.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Wishing Pills
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The wishing pills can only be used by counting seventeen by twos.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: Not unless we can count seventeen by twos,

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Gump
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The Gump's eyes are made of glass.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: the Gump’s eyes were of glass and could not be injured.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The Scarecrow's mouth is painted on.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.quote: my mouth is painted on, and there’s no swallow connected with it,

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-19-dr-niki.statement: The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman are friends.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Woggle-Bug
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: The Woggle-Bug found two handsome bracelets of wrought gold.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: The Woggle-Bug found two handsome bracelets of wrought gold, which fitted his slender arms very well.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: The Scarecrow fitted a ring to each finger and each thumb.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: Before long he had fitted a ring to each finger of his padded gloves, and not being content with that display he added one more to each thumb.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: Tip secured a fine gold watch and placed it in his pocket.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: Tip secured a fine gold watch, which was attached to a heavy fob, and placed it in his pocket with much pride.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: Tip pinned several jeweled brooches to Jack Pumpkinhead's red waistcoat.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: He also pinned several jeweled brooches to Jack Pumpkinhead’s red waistcoat, and attached a lorgnette, by means of a fine chain, to the neck of the Saw-Horse.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: Tip attached a lorgnette by a fine chain to the neck of the Saw-Horse.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: He also pinned several jeweled brooches to Jack Pumpkinhead’s red waistcoat, and attached a lorgnette, by means of a fine chain, to the neck of the Saw-Horse.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Gump
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: The Gump rose into the air and left the Jackdaws' nest behind.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: At once it rose into the air, the great wings flopping strongly and with regular motions, and in a few moments they were so far from the nest that the chattering Jackdaws took possession without any attempt at pursuit.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: The Scarecrow left the pepper-box containing the Wishing Pills in the Jackdaws' nest.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: “I must have left the pepper-box in the Jackdaws’ nest,” said the Scarecrow, at length.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Munchkin land
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: Houses and fences in the land of the Munchkins are blue.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: and that indicates we are in the land of the Munchkins, and therefore a long distance from Glinda the Good.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Glinda
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: Red houses and fences and trees indicate the domain of Glinda the Good.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: Sure enough; the red houses and fences and trees indicated they were within the domain of Glinda the Good; and presently, as they glided rapidly on, the Tin Woodman recognized the roads and buildings they passed, and altered slightly the flight of the Gump so that they might reach the palace of the celebrated Sorceress.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Gump
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: The Gump came to rest within Glinda's gardens by the fountain.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: Gradually the Thing sank lower and nearer to the ground until at length it came to rest within the beautiful gardens of Glinda, settling upon a velvety green lawn close by a fountain which sent sprays of flashing gems, instead of water, high into the air, whence they fell with a soft, tinkling sound into the carved marble basin placed to receive them.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: The Scarecrow requested an audience with Glinda.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: we have come to request an audience with your fair Ruler.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Jinjur
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: The Emerald City is now ruled by General Jinjur, who caused herself to be proclaimed Queen.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: But the Emerald City is now ruled by General Jinjur, who has caused herself to be proclaimed Queen.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Scarecrow
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: The Scarecrow got the throne of the Emerald City from the Wizard of Oz and by the choice of the people.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: “I got it from the Wizard of Oz, and by the choice of the people,” returned the Scarecrow, uneasy at such questioning.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Wizard of Oz
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: The Wizard of Oz took the throne from Pastoria, the former King.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: “I am told he took it from Pastoria, the former King,” said the Scarecrow, becoming confused under the intent look of the Sorceress.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Ozma
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: Ozma is the daughter of Pastoria.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: “Pastoria had a daughter, who is the rightful heir to the throne of the Emerald City.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Ozma
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: The girl who owns the throne is named Ozma.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: “Her name is Ozma,” answered Glinda.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Wizard of Oz
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: The Wizard of Oz hid Ozma in a secret place and prevented her discovery by magic.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: For the Wizard of Oz, when he stole the throne from Ozma’s father, hid the girl in some secret place; and by means of a magical trick with which I am not familiar he also managed to prevent her being discovered—even by so experienced a Sorceress as myself.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Wizard of Oz
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: The Wizard of Oz made three secret visits to Mombi.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: He ate beans with a knife, made three secret visits to old Mombi, and limped slightly on his left foot.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: Mombi is now with Jinjur in the Emerald City.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: “Mombi is now with Queen Jinjur, in the Emerald, City” said Tip.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.subject: Glinda
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.statement: Glinda will march with her army to the Emerald City and take Mombi prisoner.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-20-the-sca.quote: I will march with my army to the Emerald City, and take Mombi prisoner.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.quote: for Mombi was her chief counsellor,

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.subject: Glinda
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.statement: Glinda demands that Jinjur deliver up Mombi as her prisoner.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.quote: that she must deliver up to me old Mombi, to be my prisoner.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.statement: Mombi enchants Jellia Jamb to take on Mombi's form and features.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.quote: As a result of the enchantment Jellia took on the form and features of Mombi, while the old witch grew to resemble the girl so closely that it seemed impossible anyone could guess the deception.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.subject: Jellia Jamb
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.statement: Jellia, disguised as Mombi, is led from the city gates and taken before Glinda.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.quote: Therefore Jellia, hobbling along like an aged woman, was led from the city gates and taken before Glinda.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.subject: Glinda
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.statement: Glinda transforms the disguised girl back into her proper shape.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.quote: she quickly transformed the girl into her proper shape, while at the same time old Mombi, far away in Jinjur’s palace, suddenly resumed her own crooked form and evil features.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.subject: Glinda
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.statement: Glinda marches into the city at the head of a company of soldiers.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.quote: Glinda marched in at the head of a company of soldiers, followed by the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, while Jack Pumpkinhead rode astride the Saw-Horse, and the Educated, Highly Magnified Woggle-Bug sauntered behind in a dignified manner.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.statement: Mombi transforms herself into a red rose growing on a bush in the garden of the palace.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.quote: the witch transformed herself into a red rose growing upon a bush in the garden of the palace.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.statement: The Tin Woodman plucks the red rose that is Mombi and fastens it in his tin buttonhole.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.quote: so he plucked the flower and fastened it securely in the tin buttonhole of his tin bosom.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.statement: Mombi is carried out of the city and into Glinda's camp in the form of the rose.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.quote: Mombi was thus carried out of the city and into Glinda’s camp without anyone having a suspicion that they had succeeded in their quest.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.subject: Winged Monkeys
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.statement: Glinda's forces surround the city and pitch scarlet silk tents on the greensward.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.quote: Glinda’s forces silently surrounded the city and pitched their tents of scarlet silk upon the greensward.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.subject: Tin Woodman
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.statement: The Tin Woodman is fond of flowers.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-21-the-tin.quote: the Tin Woodman, who was fond of flowers, chanced to espy a big red rose growing upon a bush;

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.quote: the seeming rose was nothing else than a transformation of old Mombi.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.subject: Ozma
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.statement: Ozma is the rightful Queen of the Emerald City.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.quote: restored to her rightful position as Queen of the Emerald City

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.statement: Mombi transformed into a Shadow and glided toward the entrance of the tent.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.quote: she immediately took the form of a Shadow and glided along the wall of the tent toward the entrance, thinking thus to disappear.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.subject: Glinda
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.statement: Glinda closed the entrance of the tent so Mombi could not escape.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.quote: with a wave of her hand closed the entrance so securely that Mombi could not find a crack big enough to creep through.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.statement: Mombi transformed from a shadow to a Black Ant.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.quote: she quickly transformed herself from a shadow to a Black Ant, in which shape she crawled along the ground, seeking a crack or crevice in which to hide her tiny body.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.statement: Mombi transformed into a huge Griffin and sprang through the wall of the tent.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.quote: made her last transformation, and in the form of a huge Griffin sprang through the wall of the tent—tearing the silk asunder in her rush—and in a moment had darted away with the speed of a whirlwind.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.subject: Glinda
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.statement: Glinda followed Mombi on the back of the Saw-Horse.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.quote: Glinda did not hesitate to follow.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.subject: Saw-Horse
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.quote: Like a flash he followed the Griffin, his wooden legs moving so fast that they twinkled like the rays of a star.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.subject: Gump
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.statement: The Gump spread its wings and mounted high into the air.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.quote: it spread its great wings and mounted high into the air.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.statement: Exhausted, Mombi as the Griffin fell forward and lay still upon the desert.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.quote: in a few minutes the Griffin fell forward, completely exhausted, and lay still upon the desert waste.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.subject: Glinda
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.statement: Glinda threw a slender golden thread over the Griffin's head and destroyed Mombi's transformation.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-22-the-tra.quote: having unwound a slender golden thread from her girdle the Sorceress threw it over the head of the panting and helpless Griffin, and so destroyed the magical power of Mombi’s transformation.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.subject: Glinda
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.quote: “You are my prisoner, and it is useless for you to struggle any longer,” said Glinda, in her soft, sweet voice.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.statement: Tip gave the word to the Gump to return to the camp.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.quote: and Tip gave the word to the Gump to return.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.subject: Wizard of Oz
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.statement: The Wizard brought the baby girl Ozma to Mombi and begged Mombi to conceal the child.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.quote: The Wizard brought to me the girl Ozma, who was then no more than a baby, and begged me to conceal the child.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.quote: because they knew that this old woman had reared Tip from childhood, all eyes were turned to where the boy stood.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.statement: Mombi enchanted Ozma and transformed her into a boy.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.quote: _Into a boy!_" said Mombi, in a low tone.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.quote: that is the Princess Ozma—the child brought to me by the Wizard who stole her father’s throne.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.subject: Ozma
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.statement: Ozma is the rightful ruler of the Emerald City.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.quote: That is the rightful ruler of the Emerald City!"

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.subject: pearl
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.statement: Glinda's magic pearl remains pure white only when truth is spoken.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.quote: Only when the truth is spoken will my magic pearl remain a pure white in color.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.subject: draught
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.statement: A powerful draught causes the drinker to forget all the magic they have ever learned.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.quote: I shall merely ask you to drink a powerful draught which will cause you to forget all the magic you have ever learned.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.subject: Glinda
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.quote: I never deal in transformations, for they are not honest, and no respectable sorceress likes to make things appear to be what they are not.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.subject: Mombi
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.statement: Mombi restored Tip to her proper form as the girl Ozma.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-23-princes.quote: from the couch arose the form of a young girl, fresh and beautiful as a May morning.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.subject: Tip
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.quote: how the long-lost Princess Ozma had been discovered in no less a personage than the boy Tip

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.subject: Jinjur
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.statement: Jinjur closed and barred every gateway of the Emerald City.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.quote: for Jinjur had closed and barred every gateway

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.subject: Jinjur
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.quote: made the former Queen a prisoner

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.subject: Ozma
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.statement: Ozma is Queen on the throne of her royal ancestors.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.quote: the accession of the beautiful Princess Ozma to the throne of her royal ancestors

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.subject: Army of Revolt
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.statement: The Army of Revolt was disbanded.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.quote: the Army of Revolt was disbanded and the girls sent home to their mothers

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.subject: Gump
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.statement: Ozma ordered the Gump taken apart.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.quote: So Ozma ordered the Gump taken apart.

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.subject: Ozma
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.statement: The Saw-Horse is Ozma's personal property.
1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.quote: The Saw-Horse, being Ozma’s personal property, was tenderly cared for

1904-the-marvelous-land-of-oz-24-the-ric.subject: Scarecrow
